c.tagline: Hanseatic Baltic port of red-brick Gothic, sandy Warnemünde, and cruise-ship days.

taxi.fareNote: Taxis are metered and reliable; you can hail one at ranks by the Hauptbahnhof and Neuer Markt or book by phone or the FreeNow app.

emergency.note: 112 is the pan-European emergency number for ambulance and fire; 110 reaches the police directly.

avoid.reason: Watch bags in Hanse Sail harbour crowds, and expect rowdy football fans around Ostseestadion on Hansa Rostock match days.

hood_desc: The historic core inside the old town, home to the red-brick Gothic St. Mary's Church, the ornate Town Hall on Neuer Markt, and the pedestrian shopping spine of Kröpeliner Straße running to the Kröpeliner Tor; best for first-timers who want the sights and the main station within walking distance.

Rostock's youthful student quarter of high-ceilinged old apartment blocks, packed with bars, galleries, indie cafes and the city's largest theatre; suits travellers who want nightlife and a creative buzz.

A seaside borough a few miles north where the Warnow meets the Baltic, with a long sandy beach, the landmark lighthouse and Teepott, the Alter Strom canal lined with fish stalls, and the cruise terminal; a relaxed base for beach days and seafood.

The district just south of the old town wrapped around the Steintor and the Hauptbahnhof, with hotels, offices and easy tram links; a convenient, well-connected base for getting around the city and region.

A leafy residential area across the Warnow from the centre, with a small marina, waterside paths and open views back to the old town's silhouette; quiet and local, a calm retreat from the tourist bustle.

water.note: Tap water is safe and of high quality, as everywhere in Germany.

transit.hours: Trams and buses run roughly 4:30 AM to 1:00 AM, with F-line night buses covering the small hours on weekends; the S-Bahn to Warnemünde runs about 4:00 AM to 1:00 AM.
transit.note: RSAG runs the city's tram and bus network, while DB Regio's S-Bahn links the Hauptbahnhof to Warnemünde and the northern suburbs; a small passenger ferry crosses the Warnow at Warnemünde to Hohe Düne.
transit.pay: Buy tickets from the RSAG app, station machines, or on board; a single ride is about 2.60 EUR (~US$2.80) and a day ticket about 5.60 EUR. The regional VVW tariff covers trams, buses and the S-Bahn on one ticket, and the Deutschland-Ticket (58 EUR/month) is valid too.

bus: FlixBus intercity coaches to Berlin, Hamburg and Stralsund
ferry: Rostock Overseas Port (Scandlines & TT-Line ferries to Gedser, Trelleborg and Nynäshamn)

transit.m: Airport shuttle / regional bus plus train to Rostock Hbf (~50-60 min, coordinated with flights)
Taxi to the city centre (30-40 min)

tip.r: Rounding up or leaving about 5-10% for good service is customary; tell the server the rounded total as you pay rather than leaving coins on the table.

food.name: Fischbroetchen
food.desc: The Baltic street classic: a crusty roll packed with pickled herring, matjes, fried fish or shrimp plus onion, gherkin and remoulade, 4-7 euros.

places.name: Rostocker Fischmarkt
places.note: Fish shop and fry kitchen in one; the harbour standard for a fish roll.

places.name: NurFisch Das Fischbistro
places.note: Small bistro repeatedly named among the city's best for fischbroetchen.

places.name: Alter Strom
places.note: Row of cutters and kiosks selling rolls straight off the boats by the harbour channel.

food.name: Mecklenburger Rippenbraten
food.desc: Roast pork loin on the bone with crackling, served with kale or cabbage, buttered potatoes and a dark gravy; heavy northern farmhouse cooking.

places.name: Zum Alten Fritz
places.note: Brewpub on the river doing regional roasts with its own unfiltered beer.

places.name: Fritz-Reuter-Stuben
places.note: Old-school Mecklenburg dining room, consistently top-rated for regional cooking.

places.name: Zur Kogge
places.note: Historic sailors' tavern hung with ship models; classic north German plates.

food.name: Matjes and pickled herring
food.desc: Young salted herring served with onion rings, apple and sour cream, or rolled as rollmops and Brathering; eaten cold with boiled potatoes.

places.name: Zur Kogge
places.note: The place to eat herring in a proper old harbour tavern setting.

places.name: Am Yachthafen
places.note: Fish platters with herring and salmon schnitzel; beer-battered squid rings are a favourite.

places.name: Rostocker Fischmarkt
places.note: Buy matjes by weight or eat it in the attached fry kitchen.

food.name: Fried Baltic plaice
food.desc: Scholle, flounder or cod dredged in flour and pan-fried whole, classically with bacon and fried potatoes; the Warnemuende Sunday plate.

places.name: Am Yachthafen
places.note: Marina-side kitchen with fish platters and homemade remoulade.

places.name: Borner Diele
places.note: Regional fish cooking that follows the season's catch.

places.name: Alter Strom
places.note: Line of fish restaurants along the channel, most with plaice on the board.

food.name: Mecklenburger fish soup
food.desc: A creamy Baltic soup of white fish, root vegetables and dill, sometimes with eel or shrimp; often eaten before the main course in winter.

places.name: Zur Kogge
places.note: Soup and eel dishes served in Rostock's most atmospheric old room.

places.name: Borner Diele
places.note: Seasonal fish menu with soups made from the day's landings.

places.name: Rostocker Fischmarkt
places.note: Cheap bowls of soup alongside the fried-fish counter.

food.name: Sanddorn cake
food.desc: Sea buckthorn, the bright orange coastal berry, folded into cream cakes and tortes; sharp and citrusy against the sweetness.

places.name: Hofcafe
places.note: Cafe known for home baking, including the regional sea buckthorn cake.

places.name: Alter Strom
places.note: Seafront cafes serve Sanddorntorte with coffee facing the channel.

places.name: Neuer Markt
places.note: Market stalls sell sea buckthorn preserves and baked goods to take away.

food.name: Rostocker Pils
food.desc: The city's own pilsner, brewed in Rostock since 1878, crisp and dry; small brewpubs also pour unfiltered Zwickel versions.

places.name: Zum Alten Fritz
places.note: Brews on site and pours the local range with a harbour view terrace.

places.name: Zur Kogge
places.note: Old tavern where a pilsner with herring is the correct order.

places.name: Alter Strom
places.note: Beer gardens along the channel, busiest in the long Baltic evenings.

food.name: Sanddorn liqueur
food.desc: Sea buckthorn from the dunes turned into tart orange juice, punch and a sweet fortified liqueur drunk as a digestif on cold days.

places.name: Alter Strom
places.note: Kiosks and gift shops sell sea buckthorn liqueur and hot punch in season.

places.name: Neuer Markt
places.note: Weekly market stalls with regional juices, liqueurs and preserves.

places.name: Hofcafe
places.note: Sea buckthorn drinks alongside the cake, indoors and out of the wind.

landmarks: St.-Marien-Kirche (St Mary's Church)
A colossal Brick Gothic church crowned by a 1472 astronomical clock that still performs its apostle procession daily at noon, Rostock's greatest treasure.
Warnemünde Lighthouse and Teepott
The 1898 lighthouse and swooping 1960s Teepott pavilion form the Baltic resort's iconic duo, overlooking broad white sands and passing cruise ships.
Neuer Markt and Rathaus
Rostock's gabled market square, where the pink Baroque-fronted town hall hides a 13th-century Brick Gothic core behind its playful facade.
Kröpeliner Tor
The grandest of Rostock's surviving medieval town gates, a 54-metre Brick Gothic tower anchoring the remnants of the old city wall.
Petrikirche (St Peter's Church)
The mariners' church whose 117-metre steeple long guided Baltic sailors; a lift whisks visitors up to the finest panorama over Rostock's rooftops.
Kröpeliner Strasse
The lively pedestrian artery linking Neuer Markt to the Kröpeliner Tor, lined with gabled merchant houses, buskers and the ornate university quarter.
Kloster zum Heiligen Kreuz (Holy Cross Abbey)
A 13th-century Cistercian convent founded by a Danish queen, now Rostock's cultural history museum with medieval altars, coins and Dutch paintings.
Universitätsplatz and University Main Building
The neo-Renaissance seat of northern Europe's oldest university, founded in 1419, facing the whimsical Fountain of Joie de Vivre.
Alter Strom, Warnemünde
Warnemünde's old channel harbour, where fishing boats, smokehouses and captains' cottages create the Baltic coast's most atmospheric promenade.
Rostock Zoo and Darwineum
One of Germany's finest zoos, famed for its polar bear tradition and the Darwineum, a living museum tracing evolution alongside gorillas and orangutans.

intl.to: Copenhagen (Denmark) - via the Puttgarden route or Hamburg

train.note: Rostock Hbf has ICE and IC services to Berlin in about 2h15 and Hamburg in 2h30, with regional trains to Warnemünde on the coast in 20 minutes. Direct trains toward Copenhagen route via Hamburg since the Puttgarden train ferry ended; check the current routing when booking. DB Sparpreis fares open six months ahead.

bus.note: Coaches use the ZOB beside the Hauptbahnhof. FlixBus runs to Berlin, Hamburg and onward to Scandinavia and Poland; the Baltic coast routes are busiest in summer. Carry your passport or EU ID card.

ferry.note: Rostock is Germany's main Baltic passenger port and the ferries here are real international transport. The Gedser crossing to Denmark takes two hours and runs several times a day; Trelleborg in Sweden is about six hours and Helsinki a full day. Ferries leave from the Überseehafen, several kilometres from the centre - allow time and check the shuttle. Book vehicles well ahead in summer.

half.name: Stralsund
half.blurb: A Hanseatic port city about an hour away preserves a brick Gothic old town on the water, connected by causeway to Rügen island.

half.name: Wismar
half.blurb: A Hanseatic town about an hour west has a UNESCO-listed old town of brick gabled houses around a large market square.

half.name: Schwerin
half.blurb: The Mecklenburg state capital about an hour away centers on a moated castle built on an island in a large lake.

half.name: Rügen Island
half.blurb: Germany's largest island about an hour and a half away has chalk cliffs, beech forests, and the Baltic seaside resort town of Binz.

half.name: Bad Doberan
half.blurb: A small town about 20 minutes away has a large brick Gothic monastery church and is the terminus of a narrow-gauge steam railway.
